thread:
jess-customer: Hey team — after our egress proxy upgrade our Redwood Private control plane mTLS calls started failing. Apps hit the control plane over 443 but get an SSL handshake failure. Happening since ~0200 UTC after the proxy reboot.

jess-customer: example curl error: \`curl: (35) SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SSL: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure\`

jess-customer: openssl s_client output (sanitized):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
SSL_connect:before/after initialization
read from 0x7f...:errno=0
139...: SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert handshake failure
no peer certificate available
```

sam-support: thanks — can you share a packet capture of the ClientHello from the client to the proxy and proxy to control plane? also confirm the client presents its cert chain when talking to the proxy (is the proxy terminating TLS?).

jess-customer: attaching truncated dump, two halves: client->proxy ClientHello shows TLS1.3 + key_share X25519 present. proxy->controlplane ClientHello from proxy->server has the key_share extension missing (looks truncated). Hex snippet (client->proxy):
```
16 03 01 02 00 01 00 01 fc 03 03 53 43 12 34 56 ... 00 3a 00 1d 00 17
... key_share ext 00 33 00 14 00 13 00 1d ...
```
proxy->controlplane snippet:
```
16 03 01 01 f2 01 00 01 ee 03 03 53 43 12 34 56 ... 00 0b 00 02 03 04
... no 0x33 key_share extension present
```

ivan-network: this looks like classic TLS inspection rewriting/stripping the ClientHello. Many middleboxes terminate TLS and generate a new ClientHello toward the server; if the inspector doesn't support TLS1.3 key_share extension properly, the resulting ClientHello can fail key exchange on the server side.

ivan-network: quick repro: try forcing the client to TLS1.2 to see if mTLS completes (this avoids key_share negotiation). run:
```
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.private:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -tls1_2 -servername control.redwood.private -state -msg
```

jess-customer: ran that — TLS1.2 forced connection succeeds, mutual certs exchanged, API calls work. So TLS1.3 path is failing only through the upgraded proxy. :eyes:

sam-support: thanks, that narrows it down. Two remediation paths: (1) configure the egress proxy to do TLS passthrough/bypass for Redwood control plane hostnames/IPs so the client presents the cert directly to our control plane, or (2) upgrade/patch the proxy TLS inspector to fully support TLS1.3 key_share and not drop extensions.

sam-support: we recommend allowlisting the following FQDNs (use your region):
- control.us-west-2.private.redwood.ai
- control.eu-central.private.redwood.ai
- control.ap-southeast.private.redwood.ai

sam-support: if you can't passthrough, collect the proxy's TLS inspection logs and the proxy vendor/version — some vendors have a "preserve TLS1.3" toggle.

jess-customer: proxy config showing inspection enabled: 
```
ssl-inspect profile "corp-inspect" {
  mode inspect
  replace_server_hello on
  client_cert forward none
}
```

tara-oncall: that config explains it — the proxy is terminating and generating a new ClientHello but not including key_share. Recommended immediate fix: switch profile for the control plane hostnames to `mode passthrough` (no TLS termination) or add an exception/allowlist for the control plane certificate pinning. After that validate with: 
```
curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://control.us-west-2.private.redwood.ai/health --cert client.pem --key client.key
```

jess-customer: made a passthrough rule for `*.private.redwood.ai` and restarted the proxy. Retried the original failing request and it's now successful. mutual TLS completes and API responses are back. :tada:

deploy-bot: automated check — post-change probe to control.us-west-2.private.redwood.ai:443 shows TLS1.3 with key_share and client cert exchange OK.

sam-support: great — leaving this thread for docs. We'll add a KB entry: "Egress TLS inspection and TLS1.3 key_share stripping causes mTLS handshake failures" with recommended steps (passthrough, vendor patch, force TLS1.2 as short-term).

jess-customer: thanks all, appreciated. Closing on our side but will follow up if anything else pops up.

ivan-network: FYI for the infra team — add control plane FQDNs to the proxy bypass list by default for Private customers to avoid this class of failure.
